Let \(J_m\) denote one nilpotent Jordan block of size \(m\). The answer is

\[
\boxed{\Psi\sim J_p^{\,p(p^2-5)/2}\oplus J_1^{\,3}}.
\]

That is, \(\Psi\) has \(\frac{p(p^2-5)}2\) Jordan blocks of size \(p\), and \(3\) Jordan blocks of size \(1\).

**Solution.**
View \(M_p(F)=\operatorname{End}(F^p)\). For the regular nilpotent \(N\), the operator
\[
D=\operatorname{ad}N
\]
on \(M_p(F)\) is the tensor action on \(F^p\otimes (F^p)^*\). Identifying \(F^p\cong F[x]/(x^p)\), this is multiplication by \(x+y\) on
\[
F[x,y]/(x^p,y^p).
\]
Since \((x+y)^p=x^p+y^p=0\), after the change of variables \(z=x+y\), this is
\[
F[z,y]/(z^p,y^p)\cong J_p^{\,p}.
\]

The trace map \(M_p(F)\to F\) is a nonzero \(F[D]\)-module map to the trivial module, so
\[
\mathfrak{sl}_p(F)\cong J_p^{\,p-1}\oplus J_{p-1}.
\]
Also \(I\in D^{p-1}\mathfrak{sl}_p(F)\): using the standard truncated-polynomial model, \(N\) is similar to \(d/dt\), and multiplication by \(t^{p-1}\) has trace \(0\), with \((\operatorname{ad}N)^{p-1}(t^{p-1})=(p-1)!I\neq0\). Hence quotienting by \(FI\) shortens one \(J_p\)-block to \(J_{p-1}\). Therefore
\[
\mathfrak g\cong J_p^{\,p-2}\oplus J_{p-1}^{\,2}.
\]

Now compute exterior squares. In characteristic \(p\), for these blocks:

\[
J_p\otimes J_p\cong J_p^{\,p},\qquad
J_p\otimes J_{p-1}\cong J_p^{\,p-1},
\]
\[
J_{p-1}\otimes J_{p-1}\cong J_p^{\,p-2}\oplus J_1.
\]

Also, because \(p\) is odd and exterior square is a direct summand of the tensor square,

\[
\Lambda^2J_p\cong J_p^{(p-1)/2},
\]
and
\[
\Lambda^2J_{p-1}\cong J_p^{(p-3)/2}\oplus J_1.
\]

Write
\[
\mathfrak g=A^{p-2}\oplus B^2,\qquad A=J_p,\quad B=J_{p-1}.
\]
Then
\[
\Lambda^2\mathfrak g
=
\bigoplus_{p-2}\Lambda^2A
\oplus
\bigoplus_{\binom{p-2}{2}}(A\otimes A)
\oplus
\bigoplus_{2(p-2)}(A\otimes B)
\oplus
\bigoplus_2\Lambda^2B
\oplus
(B\otimes B).
\]

Thus the number of \(J_p\)-blocks is

\[
(p-2)\frac{p-1}{2}
+\binom{p-2}{2}p
+2(p-2)(p-1)
+2\frac{p-3}{2}
+(p-2).
\]

This simplifies to

\[
\frac{p(p^2-5)}2.
\]

The \(J_1\)-blocks come from the two copies of \(\Lambda^2B\) and the one copy of \(B\otimes B\), so there are \(3\) of them.

Therefore

\[
\boxed{\Psi\sim J_p^{\,p(p^2-5)/2}\oplus J_1^{\,3}}.
\]
